mainTopic: The מוֹרֶדֶת (a wife who rebels against her husband): what counts as rebellion, and how the court handles it
overview: The גמרא first settles the argument about what makes a wife a מורדת: everyone agrees that refusing תשמיש counts, and the only dispute is about refusing household work. It then studies the ברייתא about the מורדת. The original penalty was a weekly cut from her כתובה. Later, רבותינו enacted four weeks of public announcements, after which she loses her whole כתובה. The ברייתא also says this applies even to a נדה, and שמואל explains why with the parable of bread in the basket. רמי בר חמא adds that the announcements are made in shuls and study halls, and that the court warns her twice. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא rules like רבותינו, and רבא objects, following רב ששת and the weekly cut. אמימר and מר זוטרא then argue whether we force a woman who says her husband disgusts her. The amud ends with a real case of רב זביד's daughter-in-law and whether a מורדת loses her worn clothes, and רב גמדא's reply continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How can an ill woman be a rebel against work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the view that a מורדת is one who refuses work, because the ברייתא includes an ill woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says rebellion means refusing work: is a sick woman able to do work?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the view that a מורדת is a wife who refuses household work (מלאכה). The ברייתא says even a חולה can be a מורדת, and a sick woman doesn't have to work anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If rebellion were only about refusing work, a sick woman could never be a rebel, since she isn't required to work. Yet the ברייתא explicitly lists a חולה. So this view seems to clash with the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A wife who rebels against her husband, refusing her marital duties
Household work a wife does for her husband
A sick woman
Fit or able to do work

phrases.english: But according to the one who says it is rebellion from work,
is a sick woman fit for work?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier testing of the two opinions about מורדת against the ברייתא's list.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that a מורדת means refusing מלאכה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes a חולה, who has no duty to work, so refusing work can't be what makes her a מורדת.

steps.title: Reframing the dispute: everyone agrees about refusing relations
steps.stepSummary: Everyone agrees that refusing תשמיש makes a woman a מורדת. The argument is only whether refusing work also does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be explained this way. If she refuses relations, everyone agrees she is a rebel. Where they argue is about refusing work. One Sage holds that refusing work does not make her a rebel. The other Sage holds that refusing work also makes her a rebel.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reframing the argument. Refusing תשמיש counts as rebellion according to everyone; the only dispute is about refusing מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, it sounded as if each Sage had one single definition of מורדת. Now the view that includes מלאכה is seen as adding to תשמיש, not replacing it. So the חולה in the ברייתא is simply a woman who refuses תשמיש, which works for both opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Marital relations
Everyone agrees, there is no dispute
Where they do argue
One Sage holds

steps.whatToRemember: Refusing marital relations makes a wife a מורדת according to everyone. The only argument is whether refusing household work also does.

phrases.english: Rather: from marital relations

phrases.aramaic: כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דְּהָוְיָא מוֹרֶדֶת.
phrases.english: everyone agrees that she is a rebel.
Where they argue is about refusing work.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: מִמְּלָאכָה — לָא הָוְיָא מוֹרֶדֶת,
phrases.english: One Sage holds: from work, she is not a rebel,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר: מִמְּלָאכָה — נָמֵי הָוְיָא מוֹרֶדֶת.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds: from work, she is also a rebel.
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוסי בר חנינא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: מִתַּשְׁמִישׁ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 1 by reframing the whole dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each Sage had one exclusive definition of מורדת, so the ברייתא's חולה was a problem for the מלאכה view.
steps.terutzMaskana: Refusing תשמיש counts for both Sages; the dispute is only whether refusing מלאכה also counts.

steps.title: The original fine: a weekly reduction of the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא itself. Each week, seven דינרים are taken off a מורדת's כתובה; רבי יהודה says seven טרפעיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the main text: a woman who rebels against her husband has seven דינרים taken off her כתובה every week. רבי יהודה says seven טרפעיקין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to quote and study the ברייתא about the מורדת in full. It starts with the original penalty: a weekly fine from her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's first rule is a gradual fine, so the כתובה shrinks each week she keeps rebelling. רבי יהודה agrees there is a weekly fine but uses a smaller coin.

keyTerms.meaning: Back to the main text itself (returning to study a source quoted earlier)
We reduce, we take off
The marriage contract and the money it promises the wife
A type of coin smaller than a דינר

phrases.english: Back to the main text: a woman who rebels against her husband,
we reduce her marriage contract
by seven dinars each week.
Rabbi Yehuda says: seven terapa'ikin.
phrases.notes: A smaller coin, so his fine is lighter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section that studies the ברייתא directly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מורדת loses seven דינרים (רבי יהודה: seven טרפעיקין) from her כתובה each week.

steps.title: The later enactment: four weeks of announcements, then she loses everything
steps.stepSummary: The later Sages voted again. Now there are four weeks of public announcements, and then a warning from the court that she will lose her whole כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our Sages voted again and decided this: they announce about her for four weeks in a row. Then the court sends her a message: 'Know that even if your כתובה is a hundred מנה, you have lost it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא reports a later decision that replaced the weekly fine. After four weeks of public announcements and a warning, the מורדת loses her entire כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old system took a little at a time. The new system gives her clear public warning, and then she loses everything at once. No matter how large her כתובה is, she loses all of it.

keyTerms.meaning: They voted again (and changed the ruling)
They make a public announcement
The rabbinical court
A sum of money worth one hundred דינרים

phrases.english: Our Sages voted again,
that they would make announcements about her
for four Shabbatot, one after another,
and the court sends to her:
Know
that even if your marriage contract is a hundred maneh, you have lost it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא with a later enactment that replaces the weekly fine.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After four weeks of announcements and a court warning, a מורדת loses her whole כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This later enactment is the main procedure the rest of this section discusses: where to announce, and when to warn her.

steps.title: Who the rule applies to
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the rule is the same for an ארוסה or a נשואה, and even a נדה, a חולה, or a שומרת יבם.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is all the same to me whether she is a betrothed woman or a married woman, even a נדה, even a sick woman, and even a woman waiting for her יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists which women can be treated as a מורדת. It includes cases where you might think relations aren't relevant right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a woman who is temporarily forbidden or unable, like a נדה, a חולה, or a שומרת יבם, can still be a מורדת. Her refusal still counts. This list is what the earlier steps and the next step are built on.

keyTerms.meaning: A betrothed woman (after קידושין, before נישואין)
A fully married woman
A woman forbidden to her husband during her menstrual impurity
A widow waiting for her late husband's brother to do יבום

phrases.english: It is the same to me whether betrothed or married,
even a menstruating woman, even a sick woman,
and even a widow waiting for her yavam.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא by listing who the enactment applies to.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מורדת rules apply to ארוסה and נשואה alike, and even to a נדה, חולה, or שומרת יבם.

steps.title: Can a נדה really refuse relations?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר יוסף asks שמואל how a נדה can be a מורדת, since relations are forbidden with her anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר יוסף said to שמואל: Is a נדה fit for relations?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא בר יוסף questions the ברייתא's inclusion of a נדה. Relations with her are forbidden right now, so what is she refusing?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that rebellion means refusing תשמיש, a נדה is puzzling, because her husband can't be with her anyway. Her refusal seems to cost him nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit or permitted for marital relations

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר יוֹסֵף לִשְׁמוּאֵל:
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Yosef said to Shmuel:
Is a menstruating woman fit for relations?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one item on the ברייתא's list from step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's inclusion of a נדה as a possible מורדת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Relations with a נדה are forbidden anyway, so her refusal seems to change nothing.

steps.title: Bread in the basket
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers that a man who knows he will be with his wife later is not like a man who has no such hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: A person who has bread in his basket is not like a person who has no bread in his basket.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers with a short parable. Her refusal hurts even during נדה, because it takes away her husband's future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being hungry with bread in your basket, knowing you can eat later, is easier than having nothing at all. A husband whose wife is a נדה knows she will be permitted soon. If she declares she refuses him, she takes that away, so her rebellion is real.

keyTerms.meaning: Bread in his basket, a picture of knowing something is available to you later
It is not comparable

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
phrases.english: One who has bread in his basket is not comparable
to one who does not have bread in his basket.
phrases.notes: He means the husband knows his wife will be permitted after her נדה days, and that knowledge matters.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דּוֹמֶה מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ פַּת בְּסַלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the reasoning through a parable
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A נדה's refusal changes nothing, since relations are forbidden anyway.
steps.terutzMaskana: Her refusal removes her husband's future access, which is a real loss, so she can be a מורדת.
steps.whatToRemember: Even a נדה can be a מורדת. Taking away a husband's future hope is a real harm, like taking the bread out of a hungry man's basket.

steps.title: Announcements only in shuls and study halls
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that the announcements about a מורדת are made only in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: We announce about her only in synagogues and study halls.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא adds a detail to the enactment: where the public announcements take place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said there are announcements but didn't say where. רמי בר חמא limits them to shuls and study halls, the places where the public gathers.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogues
Study halls

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
We do not make announcements about her
except in synagogues and study halls.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: אֵין מַכְרִיזִין עָלֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a procedural detail to the enactment of step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Announcements about a מורדת are made only in בתי כנסיות and בתי מדרשות.

steps.title: רבא supports this from the word 'שבתות'
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that the ברייתא's wording, 'four שבתות', fits רמי בר חמא's ruling. The גמרא concludes that this proves it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: The wording is also precise, since it teaches 'four שבתות, one after another.' Conclude from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings support for רמי בר חמא from the exact wording of the ברייתא. The גמרא then accepts the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the announcements are made on שבתות. On שבת people aren't out working in the streets; they gather in shuls and study halls. So the choice of שבת shows the announcements were meant for those places.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise, it supports this
Since it teaches
Conclude from it, this is proven

phrases.english: Rava said: It is also precise,

phrases.aramaic: דְּקָתָנֵי: אַרְבַּע שַׁבָּתוֹת זוֹ אַחַר זוֹ.
phrases.english: since it teaches: four Shabbatot, one after another.
phrases.notes: Here שבתות really means the day of שבת, when people gather in shul and not in the street.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רמי בר חמא's ruling from step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רמי בר חמא's ruling that announcements are made only in shuls and study halls
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's wording 'four שבתות one after another' (step 4)

steps.title: Two warnings from the court
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא rules that the בית דין sends to the מורדת twice, once before the announcement and once after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: The court sends to her twice, once before the announcement and once after the announcement.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא adds another detail: how many times the court sends a message to the מורדת, and when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא mentioned the court sending to her but didn't say how often. רמי בר חמא says there are two messages: one before the public announcements and one after them. That gives her a fair chance to stop before losing her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Twice
Public announcement

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
The court sends to her twice,

phrases.aramaic: אַחַת קוֹדֶם הַכְרָזָה, וְאַחַת לְאַחַר הַכְרָזָה.
phrases.english: once before the announcement and once after the announcement.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: פַּעֲמַיִם שׁוֹלְחִין לָהּ מִבֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second procedural detail from רמי בר חמא about the enactment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The בית דין sends to the מורדת twice: before and after the announcements.
steps.whatToRemember: The procedure for a מורדת: the court warns her, then announces about her in shuls and study halls for four שבתות, then warns her again. If she still rebels, she loses her whole כתובה.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא rules like רבותינו
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא publicly rules that the הלכה follows רבותינו, the later court mentioned in the ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught publicly: the הלכה follows our Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: A sage gives a ruling about which version of the מורדת law we follow. He picks the later version of רבותינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא had two stages. First, her כתובה was cut every week. Later, רבותינו set up public announcements for four weeks, and only after that does she lose her כתובה. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא says we follow this later system.

keyTerms.meaning: Taught publicly, as a lecture to the people
Our Rabbis: here, the later court that changed the מורדת law
The binding practical law

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly:
The halacha follows our Rabbis.
phrases.notes: 'Our Rabbis' are the later court in the ברייתא, who required four weeks of announcements before she loses her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the details of the announcement process, a practical ruling is given that this later system is the halacha.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבותינו: announcements for four weeks before the מורדת loses her כתובה.

steps.title: רבא calls the ruling absurd
steps.stepSummary: רבא strongly objects to the ruling of רב נחמן בר רב חסדא and calls it nonsense.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is absurd.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks the ruling that the הלכה follows רבותינו. He calls it an absurdity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not explain his reason here. The גמרא will soon show that he holds like the earlier rule, where her כתובה is cut each week. So for him, ruling like רבותינו makes no sense.

keyTerms.meaning: An absurdity, nonsense

phrases.english: Rava said:
This is an absurdity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the ruling just given in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's ruling that the הלכה follows רבותינו
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא holds the הלכה follows the earlier rule, so ruling like רבותינו seems absurd to him.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ruling with a great authority
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says he himself taught this ruling to רב נחמן בר רב חסדא, in the name of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to him: What is absurd about it? I said it to him, and I said it in the name of a great man. Who is he? רבי יוסי son of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ruling against רבא. He says it has a strong source, a great sage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not argue the logic. He shows that the ruling is not a new idea of רב נחמן בר רב חסדא. It is a tradition that goes back to רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, so it cannot be called absurd.

keyTerms.meaning: I said it to him
A great man, an important sage
Who is he?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to him:
What is absurd about it?
I said it to him,
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רב נחמן בר רב חסדא. He learned this ruling from רב נחמן בר יצחק.

phrases.english: and I said it to him in the name of a great man,
and who is he? Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: מַאי בּוּרְכָתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's objection in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Appeal to authority: the ruling is a tradition from a great sage
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבא thought the ruling like רבותינו was baseless
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling comes from רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא, so it has firm support

steps.title: Whose view does רבא follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what source רבא relies on when he rejects the ruling like רבותינו.
steps.simpleTranslation: And whose view does he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבא's opinion comes from. This line sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא rejected the ruling without giving a source. The גמרא wants to know which earlier authority supports his position.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view does he hold?

phrases.english: And he, whose view does he hold?
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבא, who called the ruling absurd.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the basis of רבא's objection from step 12.

steps.title: רבא follows רב ששת's rulings
steps.stepSummary: רבא's view comes from רב ששת. In both versions of רב ששת's ruling, the earlier rule of cutting her כתובה weekly stays in force.
steps.simpleTranslation: As was stated: רבא said in the name of רב ששת: The הלכה is that we consult with her. רב הונא בר יהודה said in the name of רב ששת: The הלכה is that we do not consult with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבא is following רב ששת. There are two reports of what רב ששת said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two reports argue only about whether בית דין talks with her to convince her to stop. Both keep the earlier rule, where her כתובה is reduced every week. That is why רבא rejects the ruling like רבותינו.

keyTerms.meaning: Like that which was stated
We consult with her, try to talk her into stopping
We do not consult with her

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רב ששת's two versions are about whether she loses her כתובה. Both agree it is cut weekly, under the earlier rule. They argue only about consulting with her.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא holds like the earlier rule, cutting the כתובה weekly, based on רב ששת. רב נחמן בר רב חסדא holds like the later rule of רבותינו.

phrases.english: Like that which was stated:
Rava said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
The halacha is that we consult with her.
phrases.notes: He means בית דין talks with her to get her to change her mind, while her כתובה is still cut each week.

phrases.aramaic: רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda said in the name of Rav Sheshet:
The halacha is that we do not consult with her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבא follows רב ששת, whose rulings in both versions assume the earlier rule of weekly reduction of the כתובה.

steps.title: What exactly is a מורדת?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new question: what kind of case counts as a מורדת?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case of a rebellious wife?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It asks what kind of refusal makes a woman a מורדת, and sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the גמרא discussed how the מורדת is penalized. Now it asks which woman is in this category at all, based on her reason for refusing.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
A wife who refuses to live with her husband

phrases.english: What is the case of a rebellious wife?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the penalty to defining the case itself.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact circumstances that define a מורדת

steps.title: אמימר: a מורדת wants him but is hurting him
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says a מורדת is a woman who wants her husband but refuses him in order to cause him pain. If she says he disgusts her, we do not force her.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: It is where she says, 'I want him, but I am making him suffer.' But if she said, 'He is disgusting to me,' we do not force her.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר defines the מורדת. He also says that a woman who truly cannot stand her husband is not pushed to stay with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case depends on her reason for refusing. If she is refusing just to hurt him, the penalties apply. If she is truly disgusted by him, בית דין does not pressure her to stay.

keyTerms.meaning: I am causing him pain
He is disgusting to me
We force, we pressure

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
It is where she says, "I want him,
but I am making him suffer."
But if she said, "He is disgusting to me,"
we do not force her.
phrases.notes: He means we do not pressure her to stay with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A מורדת is a woman who wants him but refuses him in order to hurt him. A woman disgusted by him is not forced.

steps.title: מר זוטרא: we force her even if she says he disgusts her
steps.stepSummary: מר זוטרא disagrees with אמימר and holds that even a woman who says he disgusts her is forced to stay.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר זוטרא said: We force her.
steps.whatsHappening: מר זוטרא argues with אמימר about the woman who says her husband disgusts her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree about the woman who refuses him in order to hurt him. They argue only about the woman who claims disgust. אמימר says we do not force her, and מר זוטרא says we do.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who disagrees with אמימר here

phrases.english: Mar Zutra said:
We force her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of אמימר's statement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even a woman who says 'he is disgusting to me' is forced to stay with him.

steps.title: A story: מר זוטרא forced a woman and a great sage was born
steps.stepSummary: There was a case where מר זוטרא forced such a woman, and רבי חנינא מסורא was born from that couple.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was an incident, and מר זוטרא forced her, and from them came רבי חנינא מסורא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story that seems to support מר זוטרא. His forcing led to a good result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that forcing her did not lead to something bad. A great sage was born from that marriage, which seems to show that מר זוטרא's approach was right.

keyTerms.meaning: An actual incident, a real case
He forced her

phrases.english: There was an incident
and Mar Zutra forced her,
phrases.notes: This was a woman who said her husband disgusted her.

phrases.english: and from that came Rabbi Chanina of Sura.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a real case that seems to support מר זוטרא from step 18.
steps.raayaObject: מר זוטרא's view that we force her
steps.raayaSupportSource: The good outcome of his ruling: the birth of רבי חנינא מסורא

steps.title: Rejected: that outcome was special help from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. The good result in that story came from special help from Heaven, so it does not prove forcing is right.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not so: there it was help from Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof from the story. It says that case was unusual.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The good result came only from special help from Heaven. Normally, nothing good comes from forcing a woman who is disgusted by her husband, so the story cannot be used to support forcing her.

keyTerms.meaning: But that is not so
Help from Heaven

steps.whatToRemember: A real story only proves a rule if its result is normal. Here the good outcome was a special gift from Heaven, so it is not a proof for forcing a woman who says her husband disgusts her.

phrases.english: But that is not so:
there it was help from Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא הִיא: הָתָם סִיַּיעְתָּא דִשְׁמַיָּא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the story, not מר זוטרא's opinion itself
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The good result was a special case of help from Heaven, not a normal outcome of forcing

steps.title: A real case: רב זביד's daughter-in-law rebels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a story. רב זביד's daughter-in-law became a מורדת while she had one of her garments in hand. Four sages were sitting together.
steps.simpleTranslation: The daughter-in-law of רב זביד rebelled against her husband, and she was holding a certain garment. אמימר, מר זוטרא and רב אשי were sitting, and רב גמדא was sitting with them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting the scene for a real case about a מורדת. Nothing is ruled yet. It is preparing the next move, where the sages give their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The detail that she was holding a garment is the key to the story. It raises the question of whether a rebelling wife may keep the clothes she brought into the marriage. The list of sages tells us who will discuss the case.

keyTerms.meaning: His daughter-in-law (his son's wife)
She rebelled, meaning she became a מוֹרֶדֶת
A garment or piece of clothing

phrases.english: The daughter-in-law of Rav Zevid rebelled,
she was holding a certain garment.

phrases.aramaic: יְתֵיב אַמֵּימָר וּמָר זוּטְרָא וְרַב אָשֵׁי,
phrases.english: Ameimar, Mar Zutra and Rav Ashi were sitting,
and Rav Gamda was sitting with them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the debate over who counts as a מורדת, the גמרא turns to a real case of a מורדת and what happens to her property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setup only: a real case of a מורדת holding her garment comes before the sages.

steps.title: The sages rule she loses her worn clothes
steps.stepSummary: The three sages rule that a wife who rebels loses even her worn clothes that still exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sat and said: If she rebelled, she loses her worn clothes that still exist.
steps.whatsHappening: The sages give their ruling. A מורדת loses her right to the worn clothes she brought into the marriage, even though they still exist.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, worn clothes from a wife's dowry that still exist belong to her. The sages say rebelling costs her even these. That means the garment in her hands would go to her husband's side, which is רב זביד's family.

keyTerms.meaning: Her worn-out clothes, the items from her dowry that have been used
Still in existence, not used up
She lost (her right to them)

phrases.english: They sat and said:
If she rebelled, she lost her worn clothes that are still in existence.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the sages' ruling on the case set up in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מורדת loses her worn clothes (בלאות) that still exist.

steps.title: רב גמדא objects: are you flattering רב זביד?
steps.stepSummary: רב גמדא challenges the ruling. He says they may be favoring רב זביד because he is great, since רבא asked this question and never answered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב גמדא said to them: Because רב זביד is a great man, you flatter him? But didn't רב כהנא say that רבא asked this as a question and did not resolve it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב גמדא attacks the sages' ruling. They decided something that רבא himself left unanswered, and their decision happens to favor an important man's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge has two parts. First, the question was officially open, because רבא never resolved it. Second, ruling against the wife helps רב זביד's son keep the garment. So it looks like respect for רב זביד tipped the scale, and a judge must not do that.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, an important scholar
You flatter, you show favoritism
He asked it as an open question
He resolved, he answered

steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches that a בית דין may not settle an unresolved question in a way that favors an important person.

phrases.english: Rav Gamda said to them:
Because Rav Zevid is a great man,
you flatter him?
phrases.notes: Ruling that she loses the clothes helps רב זביד's family, since his son keeps them.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Kahana say:
Rava asked this as a question, and did not resolve it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּרַב זְבִיד גַּבְרָא רַבָּה, מַחְנִיפִיתוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling given in step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: The sages' ruling that a מורדת loses her worn clothes that still exist.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא left this question unresolved, so deciding it, and in favor of an important man's family, looks like flattery.

steps.title: Second version: the sages ruled she does not lose them
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives another version of the story. In this version the sages ruled that a מורדת does NOT lose her worn clothes, and רב גמדא begins to respond.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are those who say: they sat and said, if she rebelled, she does not lose her worn clothes that still exist. רב גמדא said to them:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second report of the same story, with the opposite ruling. It ends just as רב גמדא starts to speak, which sets up his response on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version the sages ruled in the wife's favor, so she keeps the garment. That is the opposite of step 22, and this time the ruling goes against רב זביד's family. רב גמדא's reply continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: There are those who say, introducing another version of the story

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new case. It is the same story told a second way, with the opposite ruling.

phrases.english: There are those who say,
they sat and said,
If she rebelled, she did not lose her worn clothes that are still in existence.
Rav Gamda said to them:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Retells the story from steps 21-23 with the opposite ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, a מורדת does not lose her worn clothes that still exist.
